sections.title: Project
sections.body: Avue Technologies: Maia / HRIT, AI-native GovTech talent platform in AWS GovCloud (FedRAMP context).

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Legacy HR tooling and high compliance boundaries (DoD, multi-tenant agencies) with limited direct end-user research access.

sections.title: Daniel’s role
sections.body: Senior product design on conversational workflows, SmartMatch-style recommendations, role-based interfaces, and partnership with AI/ML and engineering on explainability and guardrails.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Structured guardrails behind the LLM; progressive disclosure on recommendations; separation of automation from human hiring decisions; modular patterns for multi-tenant deployment.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body: Case study frames adoption, task completion, and trust for hiring managers (partner context). No public client UI beyond portfolio narrative.

sections.title: Project
sections.body: Avue: Maia Design System for conversational AI on the HRIT multi-tenant platform (DoD agencies, desktop-first, high-security GovTech).

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Drift between Figma and code on a complex product; legacy component library needed modernization for scale and cross-team consistency.

sections.title: Daniel’s role
sections.body: Led redesign and implementation of the Maia Design System (~3 months): design execution, cross-team collaboration, and component library modernization.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Design token pipeline (color, typography, spacing, icons). Variants and booleans for maintainable components. Figma merged into Storybook as single source of truth; Figma MCP to Cursor for typed React components and stories with one-to-one variant props.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body: Unified visual foundations, AI-adaptive interaction patterns, and faster design-to-code iteration. Documented on the Maia case study with Storybook and token examples.

sections.title: Project
sections.body: Allied Credit Union / Mahalo Banking: mobile banking redesign (FinTech, iOS and Android).

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Members need trusted, accessible mobile journeys; auth flows must balance security with low abandonment.

sections.title: Daniel’s role
sections.body: Competitive audit, core flows, and member journey UX with product and engineering on Mahalo-aligned delivery.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Tiered authentication (passcode, biometrics, security questions). Explicit tradeoffs in the case study, e.g. “Use passcode instead” at key steps to reduce drop-off.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body: Framed around member task completion and engagement; Lean UX cycles with Allied stakeholders under a fixed delivery window.

followUps: How do you mitigate auth friction?

sections.title: Project
sections.body: Juice Up, Coral Springs: DTC rebrand, owned web checkout, iOS and Android apps.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: High-intent guests leaving juiceupeats.com for marketplaces at pay; fragmented digital ordering and loyalty.

sections.title: Daniel’s role
sections.body: Lead product designer and design engineer: brand, checkout and catering flows, mobile UX, and implementation.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Owned Stripe path on juiceupeats.com; shared menu, payments, and kitchen tickets with native apps; in-app tiered loyalty on owned ordering.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body: Owner-reported ~20% higher online pickup revenue on owned surfaces after checkout shift; ~25% growth in digital revenue base after loyalty migration (scoped in the case study).

sections.title: Project
sections.body: URC Records: 0→1 e-commerce for an underground dance vinyl label.

sections.title: Problem
sections.body: Collectors need fast discovery (BPM/key), reliable inventory, and simple checkout without marketplace friction.

sections.title: Daniel’s role
sections.body: End-to-end product design and build: storefront, auth, checkout, and ops handoff.

sections.title: Approach
sections.body: Supabase auth, Stripe checkout, webhook-driven inventory, metadata-forward PLP for known buyers.

sections.title: Outcomes
sections.body: Live storefront and checkout on the case study; solo ship from concept through launch.

sections.title: Background
sections.body: Product designer across B2C, B2B, and SaaS (~4+ years), often as lead product designer and design engineer.

sections.title: Domains
sections.body: FinTech (Mahalo/Allied), GovTech (Avue Maia/HRIT), DTC and studio builds (Juice Up, URC), plus confidential HealthTech patterns on the portfolio.

sections.title: How he works
sections.body: Brand and UX through flows that ship: React, design systems, owned checkout, mobile. Strong cross-functional work with product, engineering, and compliance on enterprise work; solo 0→1 on Juice Up and URC.

sections.title: On this site
sections.body: Case studies follow portfolio grid order: enterprise (Maia/HRIT, design system, Allied), then solo builds (Juice Up, URC).

sections.title: Principle
sections.body: Daniel separates claims by source and labels owner-reported lifts explicitly.

sections.title: Sources
sections.body: Stripe and kitchen tickets (revenue), Vercel Analytics and Microsoft Clarity (web funnel), store consoles (mobile installs), partner context for GovTech and banking.

sections.title: Juice Up example
sections.body: ~20% online pickup and ~25% digital base tied to loyalty migration are owner-reported; web checkout gains are not attributed to the app alone.

sections.title: Enterprise
sections.body: GovTech and banking narratives emphasize task completion and adoption with stakeholder context, not inflated attribution.

intents.answer:
Juice Up catering on the owned site: packs and bulk ordering stay on juiceupeats.com with the same Stripe path as pickup.

Flows emphasize clear pack sizing, pickup scheduling, and kitchen-ticket handoff so back-of-house sees one order stream.
followUps: What changed in the checkout funnel?

intents.answer:
On the Juice Up case study page, mobile no longer uses a touch carousel for hero shots. react-slick handlers were blocking vertical page scroll on iOS/Android.

Below the md breakpoint the study uses a static stacked image list; desktop keeps the carousel.

Problem: guests leaving juiceupeats.com for Toast, DoorDash, or Uber Eats at Order Now.

Fix: menu → cart → embedded Stripe → confirmation and kitchen tickets on one surface. Guest checkout, pickup scheduling, counter-ready order numbers.

Cross-project pattern: document tokens and components, align Figma with code, Radix-style primitives for accessible UI, and distinguish what shipped vs. PoC.

For Avue-specific depth, see Avue: Maia design system.

Some employer work stays confidential. The portfolio uses anonymized diagrams, outcome framing, and password-gated prototypes rather than publishing client UI.

Ask Daniel in a live conversation for depth beyond the site.
